methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free community AI workshops in Hampton Roads signal grassroots capacity-building that could enable distributed peer learning networks, explicitly targeting the technology gap rather than waiting for platform solutions or institutional intervention.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU's partnership with AI Ready RVA concentrates institutional resources and expertise in Richmond's education corridor, deepening metro capability but relying on hub-based diffusion models that may not reach rural regions without intentional distribution mechanisms.

signals.title: TAYLOR: AI data centers increase Virginia’s urban-rural divide - The Cavalier Daily
signals.signal_reading: Explicit acknowledgment that AI data center infrastructure is increasing Virginia's urban-rural divide signals concentration of economic benefits in NoVA while rural areas bear environmental costs without capability gains—the core dynamic of scenario four.

signals.title: Tony Stark’s J.A.R.V.I.S., meet Amelia, Norfolk Naval Shipyard’s IT AI help assistant - MilitaryNews.com
signals.signal_reading: Norfolk Naval Shipyard deploying an AI assistant ('Amelia') demonstrates deep technical implementation in defense-adjacent Hampton Roads, reinforcing the region's specialized AI capabilities in military/maritime contexts rather than broad civilian workforce adoption.

signals.title: University of Mary Washington Adds Virginia’s First Master’s Degree in AI in Business - Northern Virginia Magazine
signals.signal_reading: Virginia's first AI-focused master's degree at UMW concentrates advanced educational infrastructure in the NoVA region, creating credentialing pathways that deepen metro expertise while potentially drawing talent away from underserved regions lacking equivalent programs.
